messages:
Alex: noticed a step-change in batch token/sec after last runtime deploy (~1862340000). overall qps looks stable but per-gpu token/sec down ~18% and avg batch_utilization fell from 74% -> 53%.
Maria: hmm. did kernel selection change in that deploy? any fallbacks to generic kernels?
Alex: yes, runtime rolled autokernel v2. there was a fallback case for some seq_len distributions where it used the generic matmul kernel. stack trace from profile attached in thread (summary below).
Jamal: can you paste the perf probe / perf counters? quick checks: seq_len histogram, avg tokens per request, queue_depth p50/p95.
Alex: pasted small snippets: ```
# perf-sample
model: gpt-medium-v1
time_window: last_1h
avg_tokens_per_request: 72
p50_seq_len: 40
p95_seq_len: 210
avg_batch_fill: 0.53
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.91
kernel_variant_breakdown: {autokernel_v2: 62%, generic_cuda: 38%}
```
Sophie: oh that kernel_variant breakdown is the smoking gun. when generic_cuda is used throughput drops, batching heuristics don't compensate because they expect stronger per-token throughput.
Maria: we should add kernel_variant tag to batch telemetry panels. currently dashboards only show batch_size and token/sec aggregated across all kernels.
Jamal: agreed. proposed new metrics/panels:
 - batch_utilization (tokens_sent / tokens_capacity) by kernel_variant
 - queue_depth (requests) by priority and age buckets
 - tokens/sec per-GPU and per-kernel_variant
 - kv_cache_miss_ratio per model+route
 - avg_queue_wait_time p50/p95

Kevin: +1. also add an alert: token/sec drop >15% sustained for 5m AND batch_utilization <60% -> pager.
Alex: adding a Grafana query prototype for batch_utilization by kernel (flux-ish):
```
sum(rate(tokens_sent[1m])) by (kernel_variant) / sum(rate(tokens_capacity[1m])) by (kernel_variant)
```
Maria: for kv cache: add metric `kv_cache_miss_ratio = misses / requests_with_kv` and surface in rollout dashboards. eviction spikes correlate with regen which increases tokens/sec.
Sophie: small experiment idea: force autokernel_v2-only for a canary shard and compare tokens/sec and avg_latency. Jamal can run it on 2 GPUs.
Jamal: I can spin up canary. need labels in telemetry to split canary vs prod. add label runtime.canary=true to the canary pool.
Alex: will push a quick telemetry tagging change: add `kernel_variant`, `runtime_pool`, `route`, `seq_len_bucket` to the batch metrics export. also instrument `batch_wait_queue_age_ms` and `batch_formed_tokens`.
Kevin: timeline? we need this in dashboards before next customer rollout.
Alex: ETA for tagging PR: EOD today. Grafana panels + alerts by tomorrow AM. canary run by EOD tomorrow.
Maria: question about queue policies: current policy is FIFO with seq_len-aware batching. maybe switch to prefer short sequences when queue_depth > threshold to keep batch_fill high. but risk higher tail latency for long seqs.
Sophie: we could try token-budget target per-batcher: target 4096 tokens per batch, but cap per-request concat to avoid stragglers. adaptive: reduce target when p95 queue_wait_time > 200ms.
Jamal: we'll run A/B: (1) current policy, (2) prefer-short policy, (3) token-budget adaptive. collect: batch_utilization, queue_wait_time p95, kv_cache_miss_ratio, tokens/sec.
Alex: note from profile: the generic_cuda kernel spends 37% more time in GEMM and has poorer memory layout for KV cache read patterns. adding kernel tagging will let us correlate.
deploy-bot: deploy v2.18.3 to runtime-cluster-3 started by @alex at 2026-03-17T14:05:09Z :construction:
Sophie: please ensure we annotate the deploy in the dashboard as a vertical line so we can correlate regressions.
Maria: I'll mock up a dashboard layout: top row: tokens/sec by kernel_variant; row2: batch_utilization + avg_batch_fill; row3: queue_depth and queue_wait_time; row4: kv_cache_miss_ratio and kernel_variant share.
Kevin: also add a lightweight daily report email for top 10 routes with lowest batch_utilization.
Alex: logging checklist for PR:
 - add kernel_variant label on metrics
 - emit avg_batch_fill, batch_formed_tokens, batch_wait_queue_age_ms
 - kv_cache_miss_ratio per-route
 - annotate deploys in metrics stream

Jamal: I'll start the canary once labels are live. will post results here and attach CSV with before/after.
Alex: thanks all. if we see generic_cuda still high after canary, next step is revert autokernel change and roll different kernel heuristics.
Maria: +1. keeping this thread as source for dashboards/alert specs.
Sophie: tagging #incidents if pager fires.
Kevin: thanks team :thumbsup:
